
### C and cache misses (3) {.smaller}


```c
int array[8]; /* assume aligned */
...
int even_sum = 0, odd_sum = 0;
even_sum += array[0];
even_sum += array[2];
even_sum += array[4];
even_sum += array[6];
odd_sum += array[1];
odd_sum += array[3];
odd_sum += array[5];
odd_sum += array[7];

```
 

* [Assume everything but `array` is kept in registers (and the compiler does not do anything funny).]{.my-small}
* How many data cache misses on a <em>2</em>-set direct-mapped cache with 8B blocks?

### assigning blocks to sets

![](/caching-code/texfig/arrayMissesWarmupBigBlocks.figure.svg){fig-alt="the array is divided into cache blocks: array[0], array[1] into a block with set index 0; array[2], array[3] into a block with set index 1; array[4], array[5] into a block with set index 0; array[6], array[7] into a block with set index 1, etc."}

*  block of memory maps to set 0, then set 1, then set 0, then set 1
   *  if more sets in cache would be: set 0, set 1, set 2, ... set N, set 0, set 1, ...
*  could be that array[0] is in set 1, not 0
   *  would just swap sets 0 and 1 --- same accesses otherwise
   *  no change to miss rate
